title: Air Florida 90
summary: Boeing 737 crashed into the 14th Street Bridge over the Potomac River after takeoff from Washington National Airport on a snowy day. The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems despite heavy snow and below-freezing temperatures, resulting in iced engine inlet sensors. This produced false low engine pressure ratio readings of 1.70 instead of the required 2.04 for takeoff. The aircraft departed with insufficient power and struck the bridge, destroying 97 feet of guard rail before plunging into the icy river. The investigation determined the pilots lacked experience in snowy conditions and failed to follow critical pre-flight procedures.
probable_cause: The pilots failed to activate engine anti-ice systems in freezing conditions with heavy snow, which allowed ice to accumulate on engine inlet probes. False EPR readings indicated insufficient thrust was set, but the pilots nonetheless proceeded with takeoff. The crew's lack of experience flying in snowy weather and failure to follow proper procedures led to insufficient power for flight and crash into the Potomac River.

factors.evidence: Pilots did not activate engine anti-ice systems despite well-below freezing temperatures and heavy snow falling during takeoff roll.
False EPR readings provided by iced engine inlet sensors indicated insufficient power was set, with actual EPR of 1.70 versus required 2.04.
Captain had made only eight takeoffs in snowy conditions on 737, first officer had flown in snow only twice.
Aircraft struck bridge immediately after takeoff with insufficient power to maintain altitude and clear obstacles.
Aircraft struck the 14th Street Bridge, hitting seven occupied vehicles and destroying 97 feet of guard rail before plunging into Potomac River.

events.text: Aircraft experiences trouble leaving gate when ground tug cannot get traction on icy ramp, crew attempts powerback using reverse thrust for 30-90 seconds without success.
Ground tug equipped with snow chains is used to push aircraft back from gate after failed powerback attempt.

Aircraft waits in taxi line for 49 minutes before reaching takeoff runway while more snow and ice accumulate on wings, crew aware of accumulation but decides not to return for deicing to avoid further delay.
Despite below-freezing temperatures and heavy snow falling, crew does not activate engine anti-ice systems that would prevent sensor and inlet ice accumulation.
Engine pressure ratio thrust indicators show false reading of 1.70 EPR instead of required 2.04 EPR due to iced engine inlet probes, aircraft unable to generate sufficient power for normal climb.
Aircraft strikes the 14th Street Bridge over Potomac River just after takeoff, hitting seven occupied vehicles on the bridge and destroying 97 ft of guard rail.
Aircraft strikes 14th Street Bridge over Potomac River, hits seven occupied vehicles and destroys 97 feet of guard rail before plunging into icy river.
Aircraft submerged in Potomac River in freezing conditions, four passengers and one flight attendant rescued by civilians and professionals, one additional passenger died assisting rescues.

title: VASP 168
summary: Flying at night from Rio to Fortaleza, Flight 168 was cleared to descend from 33,000 ft to 5000 ft. The captain, possibly disoriented by bright city lights, kept descending through the clearance limit. The aircraft struck a wooded mountainside at 2500 ft despite two ground proximity warning system activations and co-pilot warnings.
probable_cause: The captain continued descent well below the 5000 ft clearance limit, disoriented by bright lights from the city, ignoring terrain warnings until impact.

factors.evidence: the captain, possibly disoriented due to bright lights from the city ahead, continued the descent
bright lights of Fortaleza city visible in front caused disorientation
aircraft descended through its 5000 ft clearance limit and kept descending
captain and co-pilot continued descent despite being warned twice by ground proximity warning system
aircraft struck a wooded mountainside at 2500 ft and crashed

events.text: Flight 168 cleared to descend from flight level 330 to 5,000 ft over Fortaleza
Aircraft began descending through 5000 ft clearance limit while at night with city lights visible
Ground proximity warning system activated for first time
Aircraft continued descending despite GPWS warning and co-pilot warning of terrain
Aircraft struck wooded mountainside at 2500 ft and crashed

title: Aeroflot 8641
summary: The Yak-42 encountered a catastrophic stabilizer failure while descending near Mazyr. At 10:51:30 the horizontal stabilizer angle sharply increased beyond its 2° limit, inducing severe negative g-forces. Despite pilots pulling back on the yoke, the aircraft entered a steep dive and rolled 35°, disintegrating at 5700 m altitude.
probable_cause: Spontaneous movement of the stabilizer was due to disconnection of the jackscrew assembly caused by deterioration of the 42M5180-42 thread-nuts due to structural imperfections in the mechanism.

factors.evidence: the stabilizer did not respond to commands and the plane continued diving, caused by disconnection of the jackscrew assembly
failure resulted from flaws in the Yak-42's design due to metal fatigue in the thread-nuts
the autopilot switched off after 3 seconds of the stabilizer malfunction
aircraft disintegrated at 10:51:50 at an altitude of 5700 m in a steep dive

events.text: Autopilot brought stabilizer angle to 0.3° to begin descent
Stabilizer angle sharply increased exceeding 2° limit within half a second, inducing negative g-force of -1.5 g
Autopilot switched off after 3 seconds; pilots pulled back on yoke trying to level the aircraft
Aircraft rolled 35° left in dive achieving 50° nose-down attitude with over -2 g overload and disintegrated

title: Pan Am 759
summary: Pan Am Flight 759 crashed in Kenner, Louisiana, minutes after takeoff when the Boeing 727 encountered a microburst that produced a downdraft and decreasing headwind. The aircraft lifted off and climbed briefly then began to descend, striking trees. Eight people on the ground were killed. The NTSB determined the probable cause was microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff.
probable_cause: The aircraft's encounter with microburst-induced wind shear during liftoff, which imposed a downdraft and a decreasing headwind. Contributing factors included the limited capability of then-current wind shear detection technology.

factors.evidence: The aircraft's encounter with microburst-induced wind shear during the liftoff imposed a downdraft and a decreasing headwind.
At the time of Flight 759's takeoff, there were thunderstorms over the east of the airport and east-northeast of the departure end of runway 10.
The pilot would have had difficulty recognizing and reacting to the wind shear in time for the aircraft's descent to be stopped.
The aircraft struck a line of trees at an altitude of about 50 ft and crashed into the residential area of Kenner.

events.text: Flight 759 began its takeoff from Runway 10 at 16:07:57 in conditions where the winds were reported to be gusty and swirling.
Flight 759 lifted off the runway, climbed to an altitude of between 95 and 150 ft, and then began to descend.
About 2376 ft from the end of runway, the aircraft struck a line of trees at an altitude of about 50 ft.
The aircraft crashed into the residential area of Kenner, destroying a house at 1624 Fairway Street.
